title: Gradius V
subtitle: The Vic Viper returns

body: Gradius V is Treasure's PlayStation 2 scrolling shooter, published by Konami and first released in Japan on 22 July 2004. The Vic Viper travels through Bacterian territory, fighting enemy formations, large machines and hazards that fill the route ahead. Three-dimensional graphics support action played mainly on a two-dimensional plane. Open stretches alternate with narrow passages and changes of scrolling direction, asking the player to read the surroundings as carefully as the incoming fire. A second player can join the same screen for simultaneous cooperative play.

Collecting capsules advances the familiar power-up selection, letting the player decide when to activate speed, weapons or additional support. The Options accompanying the Vic Viper add more firing positions, and different weapon configurations change how they can be controlled. Holding or arranging that fire allows an attack to reach enemies while the main ship stays elsewhere. The important choice is therefore not simply which weapon is strongest: it is how its pattern fits the space, enemy positions and safe route through a particular encounter.

A collision costs a life, but the game can allow an immediate return at the point of defeat instead of always sending the player back to a checkpoint. Stage selection and score-focused play provide ways to revisit the route. Treasure's experience with demanding shooters appears in the changing layouts and carefully organised enemy patterns. Hitoshi Sakimoto supplied the score, while Hidetaka Tenjin created the cover illustration. Reviewers praised the level design and presentation, alongside warnings about the difficulty that remained central to mastering its stages.
